opportunities.title: Small Research Grants

deadlines.raw: Applications open on 12 January and close on 10 March. You will be notified in late May regarding the outcome of your application. If you apply during round 1, projects should start from early June 2026 to early December 2026.

next_open_date.raw: Applications open on 8 June and close on 8 September. You will be notified in late November regarding the outcome of your application. If you apply during round 2, projects should start from early December 2026 to early June 2027.

amount.raw: Providing up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member. Must be a PhD student or postgraduate researcher. Must work or study at a university or research institution. Must work in scientific areas within the remit of the BES. Must give a presentation if attending a meeting. Must provide a weblink to the course or conference. Must not have applied for a BES training and travel grant in the last three years.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding for new and innovative ecological research.

deadlines.raw: Applications open on 12 January and close on 25 January. You will be notified by the end of January regarding the outcome of your application. Applications should be for training and events that take place from late January to late May.

next_open_date.raw: Applications open on 8 June and close on 8 September. You will be notified by the end of September regarding the outcome of your application. If you apply during round 2, projects should start from early December 2026 to early June 2027.

amount.raw: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by contributing £30k towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member. Must be a PhD student, postdoctoral fellow, early career ecologist, established researcher, or employee of another organization. Must have employer/supervisor approval to step out of current activities during the placement period. Must have a willing host organization/department who will collaborate on the grant application. Must integrate with other disciplines and professional sectors. Must outline a key problem that an interdisciplinary approach can resolve. Must complete an in-person placement. Must require the application of ecological science or ecology as part of an interdisciplinary piece of work. Must create a learning/training/development plan that will enable the ecologist to expand their skill set. Must partner organizations show commitment to the project, either financially or in a contribution in kind.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding for the formation of new two-year synthesis groups to fast-track innovative and impactful research.
